entries.definition: The report is the research prose written for a reader of the subject: one document from a lane's text to what the run assembles at its end, named by its stage only where the stage matters — your part of the report, the report as `show report` serves it, which is the only way a seat reads it, and the copy assembled for the human reader once the run is over.

collisions.resolution: a gap a lens is about to mint keeps the word; lane text is the report
report.md at the run root is the assembled report; no seat writes blue/report.md

entries.definition: The run directory is the directory that holds one run: its record, its report and the documents assembled beside it.
The record is the run's account of every act, held as events in records/record.db, and every read a seat makes is a projection of it.

bans.variant: sitting, round, judicial, adversarial or process record

collisions.resolution: as a verb, say "put on the record" or name the verb that does it

entries.definition: A run is one research question taken from setup to its outcome.

collisions.resolution: debate.md, the Debate phase, `show debate` and the report's "The debate" section keep the word; the whole run is the run

entries.definition: An epoch runs from one chair sitting to the next: the chair asks the record who sits, the parties the record names sit, and the chair sits again.

masks.reason: a round-trip is a request and its answer, not a unit of the run

entries.definition: A sitting is one seat's dispatch, from the prompt the engine hands it to the envelope it returns.

bans.variant: your last turn, your next turn

collisions.resolution: a NULL TURN (a sitting that moved nothing on a gap) and an API turn (one model call inside a sitting) keep the word

entries.definition: A failed sitting is a sitting of a seat whose work arrives as items that closed with no envelope admitted: the call returning its envelope never succeeded, because the envelope gate refused it or its schema rejected it until the harness gave up, or its agent died; it is no turn in any gap's exchange, the engine dispatches the seat again while it owes its items, and capture names each one.

collisions.resolution: the chair's FAIL is a judgement on the board; a failed sitting is a sitting that ended without its envelope admitted, and judges nothing

entries.definition: An exchange is blue's sitting on one gap followed by its minting lens's audit of the answer, and k-max counts them.
A seat is one agent's place in the run, registered under a seat id whose role decides the surface it is given.
A side is red or blue: red audits the report and passes or fails it, blue researches, writes and repairs it.

masks.reason: quotes a wrapper heading blue must not write; the prompt names the forbidden form, not a side

entries.definition: A lens is a red seat that audits the report for one class of defect, and the only seat that files findings and mints gaps.

collisions.resolution: a lane's source method is its method, never a lens

entries.definition: The chair is red's running seat: it asks the record who sits, rules blue's motions, spot-checks the stale areas before a PASS and records red's verdict.

collisions.resolution: blue's union of the lanes' parts is a merge; the chair is the chair

entries.definition: The bench is the seat that adjudicates the contested docket, rules on motions and stamps how the run ended.

collisions.resolution: the seat ids judge, judge-terminal and judge-petition-* and the agent lead-judge keep the word; in prose it is the bench
the chair's is PASS when the board permits it; the bench's is whether remaining defect is worth remaining cost

entries.definition: A lane is one of blue's parallel first passes at the report, written by one researcher under one method.
The synthesizer is the blue seat that merges the lanes' parts into the report by union through the record's acts, and writes the report's authored surfaces.
The engine is the workflow script that dispatches the seats the record says are ready and reads the envelopes they return.

collisions.resolution: the Claude Code runtime a seat runs inside keeps the word

entries.definition: A run's lead session is the Claude Code session its live-run row names — the one that ran setup, or took the run over since — and the hooks attribute an agent to the run only when its payload's session_id is that session.

collisions.resolution: "the lead" alone is the engine's banned variant; a session that leads a run is "the run's lead session", never "the lead"

entries.definition: The operator is the person running the research, and the seat id their own commands run under.

The log is the entries a seat files for the operator with the `log` verb — a missing capability, a defect in the tooling, or friction, never a clean sitting, which is derived from having sat and filed no log entry — and none of it is debate material.

bans.pattern: \blog is (open — )?for friction\b|\bmet no friction\b|\bfriction (channel|log|footer)\b|\blog \([^)]*\) — friction\b|\b(collated|collected|aggregated|gathered) friction\b|\bfriction (so far|collected|collated|aggregated|gathered)\b|\bthe (run|sitting|seat|bench|chair)'s friction\b

collisions.resolution: `log` only ever writes; the operator reads the log with `ops log`

entries.definition: Friction is one type of log entry: something cost the seat a call, a guess or an act — a refusal, a guessed name, a misread shape, a workaround — and it notes what it expected and why, whether or not anything should change; an act no surface offers at all is a request, not friction.

bans.variant: impeded / impediment (the log read as blockage)

entries.definition: A missing capability is an act a seat needed that no surface offers, and it goes in the log, never on the board.
A citation is a source attached to a sentence of the report with the cite verb, hashed and dated so it can be checked again.

collisions.resolution: references/*.md and the proto's references option keep the word

entries.definition: A source span is the words of the source's own cached text a citation rests on, chosen by quoting them (found there once) or by naming their lines, and kept on the citation with the source's text around them; it is what the source says, and blue's reason for the citation is blue's account of it.

A source search is a read of cached sources' text for a regular expression, literal text, or a ranked hybrid query (BM25 and dense vectors), scoped to one source or across all cached sources in the run; each hit carries the source's sentence and whether a citation can quote that sentence as printed; a search across sources names each hit's source by URL and SHA256, a search of one source names it once for all its hits, and the search records nothing.

OCR-derived text is a machine's reading of a scanned document's page images: deterministic, and able to misread, so a citation quoting it records the PDF page its quote sits on and is checked against that page's image.

An anchor is the invisible token a citation, a computation, a finding or a gap leaves at its sentence in the report; a citation's or computation's is an evidence anchor, which never stands bare and may leave alone by retire, its sentence kept.

A computation is a program blue ran and recorded as evidence: its bundle, stored by its sha256, with the output and exit status of its run, and a basis — `reproducible` when two runs wrote the same bytes, `variant` when they differed and blue stated what holds across them.
A finding anchor is the anchor a lens's finding leaves at the sentence the finding is about.

collisions.resolution: the `.run-live` marker and the manual's `→ SHARED` marker keep the word

entries.definition: The verdict is the chair's PASS or FAIL on the board.
The outcome is how the run ended: VERIFIED, CEILING, HALTED or UNVERIFIED.
A finding is a lens's recorded observation of a defect in the report, or of a dispute with a gap already on the board, graded and not yet minted.
A gap is a defect in the report that changes a conclusion or a decision a reader makes, minted onto the board by a lens.

collisions.resolution: a parity gap between two numbers is ordinary English; a missing tool is a missing capability

entries.definition: A gap is material when its class is always material, or when its class goes by grade and its current severity is medium or above, and an open material gap holds the PASS gate.

collisions.resolution: material as content, or as bearing on the reader's question, is ordinary English; a gap is material only by its class and grade

entries.definition: A blocker is one entry on the list the verdict gate refuses a PASS on, with the seat whose act clears it.

collisions.resolution: `show work` marks an item blocking when the seat's sitting is not complete while it is open, and such an item is a blocker only when the verdict gate's list carries it

entries.definition: A lens's current item is the one entry of its queue it is handed in full — an item it owes, or a gap of its own the dispatch readies it on, with the items about that gap — beside an index of the rest; it stays current until the record shows it discharged, gone from the lens's work list after an act, and the next item is handed then.

A reading is a lens's recorded account of what one source did for one sentence of the report — `verify` of a citation, or of a source the lens found — with its outcome, its confidence and its reason; it reads the work unless the source was unreachable or the copy the tool stamped is not the work, and it holds nothing by itself: a gap a lens mints on it is the finding — about the citation for a cited source's defect, quoting the sentence for a found source's — and a reading that finds the source against the sentence is its lens's reading debt until that gap stands.

collisions.resolution: the OCR reading is the machine's reading of a scanned document's page images (`reading_render_sha`, `render-page`'s `reading:` line, OCR-derived text); a lens's reading is a recorded check of a source against a sentence, and a page's OCR reading may be what a lens's reading finds wrong
the verdict is the chair's PASS or FAIL; a reading has an outcome, and a reading that reads nothing is never called a verdict
a report read is the tool serving a lens the whole report; a reading is a lens's check of one source against one sentence

entries.definition: To retire a claim is to take it out of the report with the retire verb, on the record; retiring an evidence anchor alone — a citation or computation — takes it out of the report and keeps the sentence it stood on word for word, and a retired anchor is in no document.

collisions.resolution: a lens retires from dispatch, which is a state of the seat; a claim is retired from the report, on the record

entries.definition: Lens retirement is the record's state for a lens that has stopped finding material: three sittings in a row it sat through without a fresh material gap retire a lens that owes nothing on its work list — nothing new on a gap it minted since it last sat, no check it owns, no gap owed about a check of its that failed — and a head move does not ready a retired lens; a sitting that never closed is not one it sat through and counts neither way.
A stale area is the area of a retired lens whose pin is behind the report head, which the chair reads and names in a spot-check before a PASS.

A report read is the record's evidence that the tool served a lens the whole report at a head, written by the report's whole read and by no read at an anchor or a selection; it says the text was served, not that it was read, and the head of a lens's latest one in a sitting it sat through is its pin, which the lens is readied past.

collisions.resolution: a dispatch's pin is the head the chair engages a party at; a lens's pin is the head of its latest report read in a sitting it sat through, and the lens is ready while the report head is past it

entries.definition: A disposition is the bench's ruling value on a docketed gap, and it decides whether the gap closes.

masks.reason: the carry verb's flag --carried-from, and its result as the archive view prints it: a closure carried from an earlier epoch

bans.pattern: \b(gaps?|dockets?) (that )?(you|the bench) (can )?carr(y|ies|ied|ying)\b|\bcarr(y|ies|ied|ying) (the gaps?|a gap|gaps|the dockets?)\b|\b(by|you|the bench|or|may|can|must) carr(y|ies|ied|ying) (it|them)\b|\bcarried (gaps?|dockets?)\b|\bcarr(y|ies|ied|ying)\b[^.]{0,60}\bdeadlock

collisions.resolution: an inquiry's state keeps the word
`carry` is the chair's verb that restates an archived closure, and the plain English sense keeps the word; the bench REMANDS a gap and never carries one

entries.definition: Grade movement is the change a lens's regrade makes to a gap's severity, likelihood or impact, weighed as the difference in mass between the two grades in either direction, and once the open gaps' movement no docket ruling on its gap has followed totals more than 2.0 the dispatch dockets each such gap for the bench and a PASS waits for its ruling; the bench's own regrade is the grade its ruling sets and is no movement.

collisions.resolution: an exchange moves its gap when the gap's grade, its anchored text or its lineage changes, blue places a citation or computation as its answer or records a fate on its inquiry, or it closes, which is what impasse counts; grade movement is the regrade part of that alone, weighed in mass

entries.definition: A grade motion is a motion contesting a gap's grade, filed by any seat but the chair, which rules it.
Relief is the order the bench records when it grants a petition: what the seats it binds must or must not do, with whom it binds, carried from the ruling to every seat's work list.

collisions.resolution: the petitioner's ask, on the filing; relief is what the bench ordered on the ruling

entries.definition: New grounds are what a docket motion on a gap the bench ruled closed names to be admitted: an act recorded after the ruling and about the gap, located by its id or by a quote of report text an edit answering the gap wrote since, which the tool checks.
A scorecard is the numbers a seat is measured on, computed from the record: red's for the lenses and the chair, blue's for blue's seats, the bench's for the bench.

collisions.resolution: a card is one of the three scorecards, red, blue or bench, and nothing else

entries.definition: A sitting's occasion is what it was convened to do — the question put to the seat, as against the seat id, which says who was asked — and only the bench carries one, because its five sittings share a single id.

collisions.resolution: "for want of occasion" in a log entry is the plain word and keeps it; the FIELD is the one a bench register carries

entries.definition: An inquiry is one question the research could take up — proposed by blue with the hypothesis that would be true if it paid off, recorded with the fate that says what became of it — judged open while its fate is proposed or underway, which holds the PASS until blue settles it; wanting while an open material gap is about it; unchecked once settled with no check standing, which holds the PASS until the logic lens checks its latest fate; and sound while that check stands, which a new fate or any gap minted about it, material or not, unseats.

A citation or computation is reopened when an edit changes its sentence after a check and no sitting opened since has checked it — it is unchecked again; its owning lens owes the check and is the seat readied for it — the evidence lens for a citation, the lens that owns computations for a computation — a check by any lens from a sitting opened after the edit clears it, and a PASS waits until one does.

collisions.resolution: minting a successor over a closed gap reopens the gap, and a ruling's `reopens_on` says what would: neither is a reopened citation or computation

an edit's `reopened` lists every anchor its sentence change touched, of any kind, and `show work`'s `edited_since` reads it; only a citation or computation among them, checked before the edit, is reopened

entries.definition: A citation or computation is unchecked when no check of the sentence the report carries stands: nobody has checked it, or it is reopened; its owning lens owes the check and is readied for it, and a PASS waits until one is recorded.

A failed check is a standing check of a citation or computation that failed — a lens judged the computation's sentence unsound, or every reading of the citation since its sentence last changed read nothing of the cited work — which holds the PASS and is cleared by no bench ruling; it obliges the seat whose check failed to mint a gap about the anchor; a seat's close of the gap that carries a failed check is refused while the check stands, and a closing ruling of the bench closes that gap while the check still holds the PASS; and the check clears when an edit changes its sentence, when blue retires the anchor, or when the anchor is checked and holds — for a computation by the judging lens's own later check, since another lens's check beside it is a disagreement, and for an unread citation by any lens's reading of the work; and the check clearing admits the close of a gap whose check kind is source or computation only under its live-answer demand, which a live answer of that kind placed as its answer meets, as do the retire of the anchor the gap is about and the later check of that anchor by the seat whose check the gap carries that holds.

A reading debt is a lens's standing reading that finds a source against its sentence — a citation's source that refutes the sentence or says nothing of it, or a source the lens found that refutes the sentence it was read against — with no gap of its class on the subject: the lens's unfinished promise, a PASS blocker on the chair's list with the lens named, which the lens clears by minting that gap on the reading or by reading the subject again, and which blue's edit of the cited sentence, retire of the citation, or removal of the sentence a found source was read against discharges; from the mint on the gap's grade alone holds the PASS.

A gap is superseded when its own lens mints a successor naming it with `--supersedes` while it is open: that mint closes it in the same act, its purpose passing to the successor — and, for a `source` or `computation` gap that nothing answers yet, its live-answer demand, the successor carrying the same check kind — so it holds no state of its own, its fate reads superseded, and a regrade, close, carry or docket of it is refused naming the successor.

collisions.resolution: a mint naming a gap already closed is lineage and reopens it in the work's history; it closes nothing, so only the mint that names the gap while it is open supersedes it
names the gap carrying the regression a repair caused, given only with `repaired_with_regression`; that gap does not supersede the one closed
a retired claim's replacement in the report; not a gap

collisions.word: superseded (an inquiry's record or a bench statement)
collisions.resolution: a later record of the same thing standing in its place; not a gap's fate
